The evidence suggests that Methylprednisolone, which is a known inducer of B-cell Neoplasm in several contexts, may act as a mediator in the pathophysiology of B-cell malignancies. The overlapping indications between Prednisolone and Methylprednisolone imply a potential role for corticosteroids in the development or progression of B-cell neoplasms, though the precise biological pathways remain unclear. The presence of multiple indirect pathways linking Prednisolone to B-cell Neoplasm underscores the need for further mechanistic investigation to establish a direct causal relationship.
